description: Emergency POCUS interpretation corpus for the Clinical Reasoning Agent. Thirty knowledge units, each answering one clinical question, rather than thirty documents.
scope_note: Clinical knowledge only. Laboratory reference ranges are deliberately NOT here: comparing a value against a threshold is deterministic, and clinical_state.py already does it, printing e.g. 'bnp: 890.0 pg/mL <-- HIGH (ref <=100)'. Putting the same information in a retrieval corpus would make a settled comparison depend on a similarity score.
licence_note: Store a citation and a short quotation per unit. Do NOT redistribute whole guideline documents: most are copyrighted. Every unit must name where its text came from before it is used for anything reported.
how_to_use: Replace each unit whose status is 'placeholder' with real text and a real citation, then set status to 'sourced'. Retrieval returns placeholders so the pipeline is testable before real content exists, but reason() marks any answer resting on them as NOT guideline-grounded, so a placeholder can never pass as evidence.

passages.text: PASTE 2-3 SENTENCES FROM: Introduction and Technique (the six BLUE points)
Left ventricular systolic function on focused echo: how it is assessed and what reduced function implies.
Right ventricular dilation: what it suggests in the acutely breathless patient, and its limits.
Pericardial effusion: recognition, and why size alone does not determine significance.
Tamponade: the sonographic signs and their relationship to the clinical picture.
Focused echocardiography in undifferentiated shock: what a focused study answers and what it cannot exclude.
Right upper quadrant FAST view: what is examined and where free fluid collects first.
Left upper quadrant FAST view: landmarks and common pitfalls.
Pelvic FAST view: what is examined and the effect of bladder filling.
Pericardial FAST view: what it assesses in trauma.
FAST interpretation: what free fluid indicates, and the sensitivity limits of a negative study.
Classification of shock and the sonographic features distinguishing the categories.
Hypovolaemic shock: supporting sonographic and physiological features.
Cardiogenic shock: supporting features and how it is distinguished from other causes.
Obstructive shock: the causes a focused study can identify.
Distributive shock: why imaging is largely a diagnosis of exclusion here.
Structured approach to acute dyspnoea combining lung and cardiac windows.
Structured approach to chest pain: what POCUS contributes and what it cannot settle.

What a negative POCUS study does NOT establish. Written deliberately: the reasoning model proposed pathology for a patient whose scan was entirely negative, and separately treated unrelated absent findings as arguments against a diagnosis.

When a focused study is insufficient and formal imaging or specialist review is indicated.
